title: Ang 98–108: Guru Arjan in Majh
hookLine: father, mother, kin: the Lord as family on ang 103
tomorrow: how do you get rid of an 'I' that won't leave?

lines: ARE YOU SAFE? STAY ON THE LINE.
WHO IS FAMILY ALL AT ONCE?
cards: Two in the morning. A phone lights up on a kitchen counter. A driver, broken down on a dark highway, hours from home, hazard lights blinking.
The person who answers doesn't start with the truck. Are you safe? Okay.
Stay on the line. Somebody's coming. For a minute, a stranger's voice is the whole family he's got.
So who could be your father, your mother and your brother all at once? On ang 103, Guru Arjan answers in one breath.

teach.b: From ang 98 to 108, Majh holds Guru Arjan's own hymns, the grown son's voice. On ang 103 he writes to God, in paraphrase: you are my father; you are my mother. You are my kin; you are my brother.
You are my protector everywhere, so what fear, what worry, can touch me?
Then: by your grace I came to know you; you are my shelter, you are my pride. Look at the order. Father and mother come first: the ones who love you before you've done anything.
Kin and brother: the ones who show up. Then protector, everywhere, which is the reason the fear runs out. He doesn't say no night comes.
He says no night is spent alone. And notice how the hymn says he knows this: by grace, not by figuring it out. That fits the man.
Tradition remembers his letters of longing; here the longing has found its answer, and the answer is family.
It's a hymn some families teach their children, and it fits dark highways of every kind: a hospital hallway, an exam room, the night before a move.
A phone call at two in the morning has the same shape. Are you safe? You're not alone.

how: The ang 103 hymn, 'you are my father, you are my mother', is sung in kirtan and taught to Sikh children; some families recite it at bedtime or before travel.

s: the ang 103 hymn promises that nothing bad will ever happen
it says fear can't touch you because the protector is everywhere; no night spent alone.
on ang 103, Guru Arjan calls God father, mother, kin and brother
and protector everywhere, so what fear or worry?

games.q: your friend's parents work abroad for the year. at a school event she says she has no family here. what does the ang 103 hymn have for her?
o: nothing much; the hymn is about your relatives at home.
that family is only real once her parents come back.
the hymn names God as father, mother, kin and protector everywhere.
games.why: Guru Arjan's hymn makes the One father, mother, kin and brother, a protector in every place. she isn't without family here.

practice: If you can, read the hymn on ang 103 before you begin. Find a photo of people who are family to you, by blood or not, on your phone or on a wall, and look at it for the whole sit.
Let each face be one word of the hymn: father, mother, kin, brother. Then let the last word, protector, hold all of them.

wordCard.voice: Ang 98. The page where Guru Arjan's Majh hymns begin, the run that holds you are my father, you are my mother, on ang 103.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: toon meraa pitaa, you are my father; the opening of the ang 103 hymn.

carryVoice: One word to carry: family, the kind that stays on the line all night. Sleep easy.
